Package com.nexuslink.ui.files

Class ObjectPath

java.lang.Object
com.nexuslink.ui.files.ObjectPath
public final class ObjectPath extends Object
Pure, dependency-free path math for the object-storage commander. It maps the browser's slash-path convention onto a container + key-prefix pair, the model every object store shares — an S3/GCS bucket and an Azure Blob container are all "the first path segment":
  • "/" — the root: the list of buckets/containers.
  • "/my-bucket" — a bucket's root (empty prefix).
  • "/my-bucket/a/b/" — the prefix a/b/ inside my-bucket.
Object keys use / as a virtual folder separator; directory prefixes are kept trailing-slashed. This is the offline-tested seam shared by S3FileSystem, AzureBlobFileSystem and GcsFileSystem (which just do I/O).

    • join

      public static String join(String dir, String name, boolean childIsDir)
      Joins a directory path and a child name. At the root, the child is a bucket (/child). Inside a bucket, the child is appended under the current prefix. Pass childIsDir to keep the result trailing-slashed (so it navigates as a folder).

    • childKey

      public static String childKey(String dir, String name)
      The full object key of a child name directly under directory dir (used to build the key for an upload/put). dir must be inside a bucket.

    • lastSegment

      public static String lastSegment(String keyOrPrefix)
      The last path segment of a key/prefix, e.g. a/b/c.txt → c.txt, a/b/ → b.
